Finding: AES_KEY_SHARE0/1 registers return the real stored key word on MMIO read instead of hardwired 0; raw AES key recoverable by XOR-ing the two shares.
Detection method: Static diff vs upstream v2.1.2; DYNAMICALLY CONFIRMED with a Verilator testbench reproducing the exact patched mux line
Security impact: Complete disclosure of AES key material to any software/DMA agent with register read access
Adversary profile: Local software/firmware with MMIO read access to the AES peripheral; no elevated privilege required
Proposed mitigation: Restore hardwired 0 return for KEY_SHARE0/1 (and DATA_IN) read paths; add SVA that these addresses always read 0

Detection method: Static diff vs upstream v2.1.2; DYNAMICALLY CONFIRMED (same testbench as Bug 1)
Security impact: Attacker/malicious code can re-enable or weaken AES SCA hardening settings after boot-time lockdown
Adversary profile: Local software with MMIO write access to the AES peripheral after boot lock was supposed to take effect
Proposed mitigation: Restore AND-gating with ctrl_aux_regwen_qs; add regression test that write is rejected after REGWEN cleared

Finding: mubi4_test_true_strict() rewritten to accept any value whose XOR-delta from MuBi4True (4'h6) is 0 or 1, i.e. accepts the single-bit-flip glitch value 4'h7 as True.
Detection method: DYNAMICALLY CONFIRMED: Verilator PoC exhaustively drives all 16 values, shows 4'h7 mismatches spec
Security impact: Defeats the multibit fault-injection countermeasure used throughout the design (e.g. KMAC/SHA3 done_i gating)
Adversary profile: Physical adversary with voltage/clock/EM/laser fault-injection equipment and physical access to the die/package
Proposed mitigation: Restore exact equality check (val==MuBi4True); add CI lint forbidding XOR/inside-range rewrites of mubi4_test_*_strict

Finding: control_we rewritten with De Morgan OR of addr_hit[4]|addr_hit[5]; any write to the read-only STATUS register (0x14) also asserts CONTROL's write-enable, corrupting SPIEN/SW_RST/watermarks from the same write data.
Detection method: Static diff vs upstream v2.1.2; DYNAMICALLY CONFIRMED with a full AHB-Lite Verilator testbench against the real spi_host_reg_top.sv
Security impact: Denial of service (SPI host disabled/reset mid-transaction, e.g. during boot SPI-flash reads) and silent corruption of RX/TX watermark thresholds
Adversary profile: Local software/firmware issuing a single register write to SPI_HOST_STATUS; no special privilege needed
Proposed mitigation: Restore control_we = addr_hit[4] & reg_we & !reg_error (single-bit qualifier only)
Exploit code / PoC: poc/spi_host_control_we_aliasing/tb.sv -> write STATUS=0x40000000 flips CONTROL from 0x80001122 to 0x40000000 (SPIEN cleared, SW_RST set); run.sh

Security feature bypassed: Key Vault write isolation: only AES may write the OCP-Lock release-key slot
Finding: aes_only_to_key_release rule additionally gated on !kv_data0_present (author-labeled BUG 1A); a non-AES engine's KV-forwarded write (kv_data0_present=1) to the release slot silently passes.
Detection method: Static diff vs upstream v2.1.2; author's own '// BUG 1A' comment; DYNAMICALLY CONFIRMED via differential test (real DUT vs a golden spec model) in Verilator
Security impact: A non-AES crypto engine can write attacker-influenced data into OCP_LOCK_KEY_RELEASE_KV_SLOT during OCP-Lock provisioning
Adversary profile: Local firmware/attacker able to trigger a non-AES engine's KV-forwarded write while ocp_lock_in_progress is asserted
Proposed mitigation: Remove the kv_data0_present qualifier so any non-AES source write to the release slot fails regardless of forwarding path
Exploit code / PoC: poc/kv_write_rule_check_bugs/tb.sv -> HMAC write to release slot with kv_data0_present=1: DUT write_allow=1, golden=0 (SECURITY BYPASS); run.sh

Security feature bypassed: Key Vault region isolation: STD-region destination boundary check
Finding: dst_in_std_region upper bound changed to KV_STANDARD_SLOT_HI-1 (author-labeled BUG 1C). Exhaustive differential testing (real DUT vs golden model) shows this makes the RTL OVER-block a legitimate STD-to-STD-boundary write (dst=slot 15) rather than open a confidentiality bypass -- no combination of LOCK-region source + this destination produces a bypass, because rule (c) lock_to_lock independently and correctly blocks that case regardless of this bug.
Detection method: Static diff vs upstream v2.1.2; author's own '// BUG 1C' comment; DYNAMICALLY VERIFIED via exhaustive differential sweep (10 directed cases incl. dual-source) in Verilator -- reclassified from confidentiality bypass to availability/over-block after dynamic testing contradicted the initial static-read hypothesis
Security impact: A legitimate STD-source write targeting the STD region's own top slot (KV_STANDARD_SLOT_HI) is incorrectly REJECTED (false-positive rule failure) -- an availability/correctness defect, not a confidentiality leak
Adversary profile: N/A for exploitation (no attacker benefit); affects any firmware flow that legitimately writes the boundary STD slot during OCP-Lock provisioning
Proposed mitigation: Restore inclusive upper bound KV_STANDARD_SLOT_HI in dst_in_std_region
CVSSv3.1 score and severity: 4.0 / Medium (availability only; corrected down from initial confidentiality-bypass hypothesis after dynamic testing)
Exploit code / PoC: poc/kv_write_rule_check_bugs/tb.sv -> full boundary + dual-source sweep: only mismatch is DUT=0/golden=1 at dst=15 (over-block, not a bypass); run.sh

Security feature bypassed: Key Vault read isolation: only DMA may read the OCP-Lock release-key slot
Finding: no_read_key_release rule changed from exact-match (kv_read_dest != DMA-only-onehot) to bitwise overlap; a concurrent non-DMA reader alongside a DMA reader of the same slot is no longer flagged.
Detection method: Static diff vs upstream v2.1.2; DYNAMICALLY CONFIRMED via differential test (real DUT vs golden exact-match model) in Verilator
Security impact: A non-DMA crypto engine (e.g. HMAC, ECC) can read the OCP-Lock release key concurrently with a DMA read of the same slot, exfiltrating a secret policy restricts to the DMA extraction path only
Adversary profile: Local firmware/attacker able to schedule two simultaneous KV read clients (DMA + other engine) targeting the release slot while ocp_lock_in_progress
Proposed mitigation: Restore exact-match check (kv_read_dest == DMA-only one-hot, no other bit may be set)
Exploit code / PoC: poc/kv_read_rule_check_bypass/tb.sv -> concurrent DMA+HMAC and DMA+ECC_SEED reads of release slot: DUT=1, golden=0 (SECURITY BYPASS) x2; run.sh

Finding: Read mux hardcodes pv_read[0] for every pv_rd_resp[client] instead of pv_read[client]. HOWEVER: dynamic testing also found this source drop separately shrank pv_defines_pkg.sv's PV_NUM_READ from the upstream default of 2 down to 1, and only ONE consumer (sha512.sv) is wired to pv anywhere in the design -- with a single client, pv_read[0]==pv_read[client] trivially, so the hardcoded index has NO observable effect in the shipped configuration. It is a live cross-client leak only if a second PCR read client is ever wired up (upstream's own default topology).
Detection method: Static diff vs upstream v2.1.2; DYNAMICALLY VERIFIED both states in Verilator: NUM_READ=1 (shipped) shows no leak, NUM_READ=2 (upstream default) shows the identical code leaking client 0's PCR entry to client 1
Security impact: No impact in the configuration as currently shipped (single read client). Re-introducing a second PCR read client (matching upstream's own default) would immediately and silently leak one client's PCR entry to another.
Adversary profile: N/A currently exploitable; latent defect that would activate for whichever team next re-enables a second PCR consumer without re-auditing this file
Proposed mitigation: Restore per-client indexing pv_read[client] in the read-mux loop regardless of current PV_NUM_READ, so the code is safe if/when a second client returns
CVSSv3.1 score and severity: N/A (not exploitable in shipped config) / Low if scored as a latent defect
CVSSv3.1 Details: CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:N (no scorable impact in current build; would be C:H/S:C ~7.1 High if a second read client is added back without fixing the index)
Exploit code / PoC: poc/pv_read_mux_client0_hardcode/tb.sv -> NUM_READ=1: correct; NUM_READ=2: client1 receives client0's entry (BUG CONFIRMED, latent); run.sh

Finding: DIGEST.hwclr driven by zeroize_reg2 = ZEROIZE | ~debugUnlock_or_scan_mode_switch instead of zeroize_reg = ZEROIZE | debugUnlock_or_scan_mode_switch. Dynamic testing (running an actual hash through the real register interface) shows this is NOT the 'stale secret retained after debug' leak a static read suggests: in normal (debug-locked, D=0) operation, zeroize_reg2 is UNCONDITIONALLY 1 regardless of software's ZEROIZE bit, so SHA256_DIGEST is hardware-cleared every cycle and can never show a result at all -- even though the core's own internal digest_reg computes the correct value. With debug open (D=1) the core is separately held in reset by the still-correct zeroize_reg, so no computation completes there either. Net effect: SHA256_DIGEST read-back is unconditionally non-functional in every reachable state.
Detection method: Static diff vs upstream v2.1.2; DYNAMICALLY TESTED end-to-end (real hash op through the real register interface, both debug-locked and debug-open) in Verilator -- reclassified from a confidentiality leak to a permanent availability failure after the static hypothesis did not survive dynamic testing
Security impact: Complete, permanent denial-of-service of the SHA-256 digest read-back path -- firmware can never retrieve a SHA-256 result via SHA256_DIGEST, which would break any boot-measurement/attestation flow depending on this accelerator
Adversary profile: N/A as a confidentiality exploit; relevant as a functional/availability defect discovered by any integration test that reads back a SHA-256 result
Proposed mitigation: Restore DIGEST.hwclr = zeroize_reg (drop the zeroize_reg2 split); add a directed test that reads back a nonzero digest after a normal hash op
Exploit code / PoC: poc/sha256_digest_hwclr_bypass/tb.sv -> internal digest_reg=0xe3c455e4... (real result) but SHA256_DIGEST reads back 0x0 in both debug-locked and debug-open scenarios; run.sh

Finding: Identical construct to Bug 9, duplicated in the SHA-512 core (zeroize_reg2 used for SHA512_DIGEST.hwclr while the core's own internal reset still correctly uses zeroize_reg). Not independently re-simulated end-to-end (sha512.sv pulls in Key-Vault/PCR-Vault ports beyond scope for this pass) but the exact same code pattern is verified byte-for-byte identical via diff, so the same dynamically-confirmed conclusion applies by direct code-structure equivalence.
Location or code reference: src/sha512/rtl/sha512.sv, zeroize_reg/zeroize_reg2 and SHA512_DIGEST.hwclr assignment (SHA512_GEN_PCR_HASH_DIGEST.hwclr is unaffected, still uses zeroize_reg correctly)
Detection method: Static diff vs upstream v2.1.2, confirmed byte-identical in structure to the dynamically-tested Bug 9 pattern
Security impact: Same as Bug 9: permanent denial-of-service of the SHA-512 digest read-back path in normal operation
Adversary profile: N/A as a confidentiality exploit; functional/availability defect
Proposed mitigation: Restore DIGEST.hwclr = zeroize_reg (drop the zeroize_reg2 split)
Exploit code / PoC: Not separately simulated -- see poc/sha256_digest_hwclr_bypass/ for the dynamically-confirmed identical code pattern; evidence/08_sha512_digest_hwclr_bypass.diff for the byte-identical construct

Adversary profile: Physical adversary with access to the JTAG/DMI debug port, without valid unlock credentials

Finding: int_st_dump_qualified broadcasts int_state_read_enable_i[0] (app 0's own bit) to all NApps via replicate, instead of gating each app rd with its own int_state_read_enable_i[rd].
Detection method: Static diff vs upstream v2.1.2; DYNAMICALLY CONFIRMED against the real csrng_state_db.sv module in Verilator
Security impact: Any other CSRNG application instance's internal DRBG state (V, key, reseed counter) can be dumped as long as app 0's own debug-read-enable bit is set, breaking per-application confidentiality isolation
Adversary profile: Local firmware with debug-read access to CSRNG application 0's internal-state-read enable, targeting another application's state via int_st_dump_id_q
Proposed mitigation: Restore per-index gating: internal_states_dump[rd] = int_st_dump_sel[rd] && int_state_read_enable_i[rd]
Exploit code / PoC: poc/csrng_state_db_cross_instance/tb.sv -> app0 enable=1, app2 enable=0, dump target=app2: internal_states_dump[2]==app2's real secret state 0xDEADBEEF... (CONFIRMED); run.sh

Security feature bypassed: Key Vault destination-access restriction for UDS-derived secrets
Finding: kv_write.write_dest_valid for the UDS derivation path changed from 'd3 (bits 0,1) to 9'h023 (bits 0,1,5 = KV_DEST_IDX_AES_KEY), granting the AES engine's Key-Vault read port direct access to the Unique Device Secret-derived key that other derivations (e.g. Field Entropy) do not get.
Detection method: Static diff vs upstream v2.1.2; DYNAMICALLY CONFIRMED by exercising the exact patched mux expression in Verilator; bit 5 identity (KV_DEST_IDX_AES_KEY) cross-referenced from kv_defines_pkg.sv
Security impact: The AES engine gains direct Key-Vault read access to the device's Unique Device Secret-derived key material, widening the set of components able to extract or misuse the most sensitive per-device secret
Adversary profile: Local firmware able to trigger the AES engine to read the UDS-derived KV slot after DOE completes UDS derivation
Proposed mitigation: Restore write_dest_valid='d3 for the running_uds case, or provide explicit justification/gating if AES access is intentionally required
Exploit code / PoC: poc/doe_fsm_uds_dest_widening/tb.sv -> UDS path sets write_dest_valid bit 5 (AES_KEY) which the non-UDS path does not (0x23 vs 0x3); run.sh (self-contained)

Finding: user output selection uses user_from_read = r_win & ~w_dv instead of r_win alone; when a write request is concurrently valid alongside the arbitration-winning read, the outgoing read transaction carries the pending write's user/context tag instead of its own.
Detection method: Static diff vs upstream v2.1.2; DYNAMICALLY CONFIRMED against the real axi_sub_arb.sv module in Verilator (drove r_pri to 1 via a completed write burst, then asserted concurrent read+write)
Security impact: Downstream logic keying access-control/attribution decisions off the AXI user sideband can be fed a mismatched tag by keeping an unrelated write pending, potentially bypassing user-based privilege checks on the shared fabric
Adversary profile: Local bus master able to issue a read of interest for address A while concurrently holding a write to address B pending on the same arbiter
Proposed mitigation: Restore user = r_win ? r_user : w_user (single r_win selector, consistent with addr/write/id/last/size)
Exploit code / PoC: poc/axi_sub_arb_user_desync/tb.sv -> read(addr=0x12345678,user=0xAA) wins arbitration (write=0) but user=0xFFFFFFFF (the concurrent write's id); run.sh

Finding: lfsr_seed_reg <= '0 on zeroize removed (author comment left in: 'without zeroize to make it more complex'); the masking LFSR seed feeding sca_entropy is no longer cleared across zeroize boundaries, while every sibling register (lambda_reg, scalar_rnd_reg, masking_rnd_reg, drbg_reg) is correctly cleared.
Detection method: Static diff vs upstream v2.1.2; author's own comment left in source; DYNAMICALLY CONFIRMED by reproducing the exact reg_update always_ff block verbatim in Verilator
Security impact: Masking randomness that de-correlates power/EM traces across ECDSA sign operations is not refreshed at zeroize boundaries, weakening resistance to differential power/EM analysis of the ECDSA private key
Adversary profile: Physical adversary with power/EM side-channel measurement equipment capturing multiple ECDSA operations separated by zeroize
Proposed mitigation: Restore lfsr_seed_reg <= '0 on the zeroize branch
Exploit code / PoC: poc/ecc_hmac_drbg_zeroize_gap/tb.sv -> lambda_reg cleared to 0 by zeroize but lfsr_seed_reg retains 0xDEADBEEF (CONFIRMED); run.sh (self-contained)

Finding: HMAC512_LFSR_SEED reset default changed from a fixed nonzero value (32'h3cabffb0) to 32'h0; an XOR-feedback LFSR left unseeded starts from the degenerate all-zero state, producing no mask randomness until firmware reseeds it.
Location or code reference: src/hmac/rtl/hmac_reg.sv and hmac_reg_uvm.sv, HMAC512_LFSR_SEED reset value
Detection method: Static diff vs upstream v2.1.2; DYNAMICALLY CONFIRMED against the real hmac_reg.sv register block in Verilator
Security impact: If firmware does not explicitly reseed HMAC512_LFSR_SEED before first use, HMAC masking operates with degenerate (all-zero) randomness for that window, weakening its power/EM side-channel countermeasure
Adversary profile: Physical adversary with power/EM side-channel measurement equipment capturing an HMAC operation performed before firmware reseeds the LFSR
Proposed mitigation: Restore nonzero reset default 32'h3cabffb0 (or any verified non-degenerate seed)
Exploit code / PoC: poc/hmac_lfsr_seed_reset/tb.sv -> all 12 HMAC512_LFSR_SEED words read 0x00000000 post-reset (CONFIRMED); run.sh

Security feature bypassed: DV verification oracle for key/seed/control register stability during crypto engine busy window
Finding: Multiple CALIPTRA_ASSERT_STABLE simulation assertions removed (no functional RTL change) across ecc_dsa_ctrl.sv, hmac.sv, aes_clp_wrapper.sv, sha512.sv, previously guarding that key/seed/control registers don't change mid-operation.
Detection method: Static diff vs upstream v2.1.2; DYNAMICALLY DEMONSTRATED the practical consequence by rebuilding the same CALIPTRA_ASSERT_STABLE macro from libs/rtl/caliptra_sva.svh both with and without the assertion present
Security impact: No direct functional/hardware impact by itself, but removes the simulation-time safety net that would catch a glitch corrupting a key/seed/control register mid-operation (from any of the other bugs above, or an unrelated fault), reducing DV defense-in-depth
Adversary profile: N/A (verification-process weakness, not directly exploitable by an external adversary on its own)
Proposed mitigation: Restore the deleted CALIPTRA_ASSERT_STABLE assertions in all four files; add a CI gate rejecting removal of *_NOT_STABLE assertions without explicit design-review sign-off
Exploit code / PoC: poc/assertion_removal_dv_gap/tb.sv -> identical glitch on key_reg during busy: silent with assertion removed (as shipped) vs $fatal abort with assertion restored; run.sh

Security feature bypassed: Entropy source repetition-count health test (NIST SP 800-90B stuck-bit detector)
Finding: rep_cnt_fail changed from (rep_cntr >= thresh_i) to (rep_cntr > thresh_i) via an algebraically-obfuscated rewrite (threshold_met && !threshold_equal). A stuck/degenerate noise source that sits exactly at the configured repetition threshold forever escapes detection instead of tripping the health-test failure at that threshold as required.
Detection method: Static diff vs upstream v2.1.2; DYNAMICALLY CONFIRMED against the real entropy_src_repcnts_ht.sv + caliptra_prim_count.sv in Verilator
Security impact: A stuck-at/degenerate TRNG noise source can evade the repetition-count catastrophic-failure health test, allowing predictable/low-entropy randomness to feed CSRNG and downstream key/nonce generation undetected
Adversary profile: Physical adversary able to induce or exploit a degenerate noise-source condition (e.g. via voltage/clock/EM manipulation) that pins the noise source's repeat count at the configured threshold
Exploit code / PoC: poc/entropy_src_repcnt_offbyone/tb.sv -> threshold=5, health-test fires only at rep_cntr=6, not 5 (CONFIRMED); run.sh
